rules.title: Boston home rule petition for rent stabilization (H.3744, 193rd General Court)
rules.requirement: A home rule petition that would have authorized the City of Boston to implement rent stabilization. It was sent to a study order and was not enacted, so it imposes no rent cap.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have applied to residential rental housing in the City of Boston; this document does not give the specific cap or covered units.
rules.quoted_span: By Representative Montaño of Boston, a petition (accompanied by bill, House, No. 3744) of Samantha Montaño (with the approval of the mayor and city council) that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.
rules.conflict_note: The bill history shows the bill 'Accompanied a study order, see H5035' on 9/9/2024. The 193rd session ended without enactment, so the measure is treated as failed. Massachusetts state law (G.L. c. 40P) generally bars local rent control unless the Legislature authorizes it. The bill text and cap details are not in this document.

rules.title: Boston home rule petition for tenant eviction protections (H.3744, 193rd General Court)
rules.requirement: A home rule petition that would have authorized the City of Boston to implement tenant eviction protections. It was sent to a study order and was not enacted, so it imposes no just-cause requirement.
rules.coverage_conditions: Would have applied to residential tenancies in the City of Boston; this document does not give specific coverage details.
rules.quoted_span: By Representative Montaño of Boston, a petition (accompanied by bill, House, No. 3744) of Samantha Montaño (with the approval of the mayor and city council) that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.
rules.conflict_note: The bill history shows the bill 'Accompanied a study order, see H5035' on 9/9/2024. The 193rd session ended without enactment, so the measure is treated as failed. The substantive eviction-protection terms are not in this document.
